name: Ironveil Chrome-Scrap Street Set
description: This outfit is where Shelf survival meets the aesthetic of the aug-yards — the salvage zones where stripped chrome and discarded cyberware get broken down for parts. The wearer has built their look around that world deliberately. A close-fitting long-sleeve shirt in dark graphite, made from a heavy thermal weave with aug-channel seams running along both arms — the channels are empty, not functional, but the shirt was built for chrome-users and found its way down to the Shelf. Over it hangs a sleeveless vest constructed from layered strips of salvaged materials: sections of conveyor belt rubber, cut canvas, pieces of what was once a ballistic panel, all stitched and riveted together into a rough asymmetric armor-vest that sits heavier on the left side. Salvaged chrome components — a single non-functional forearm housing stripped of its internals, worn as a bracer on the right arm; a defunct sensor ring worn as a thick wrist cuff on the left — accessorize without augmenting, a visual claim on a world that's financially out of reach. Straight-leg trousers in charcoal industrial denim, the right knee blown out and re-patched with black rubber, are tucked into mid-calf lace-up boots with thick composite soles, the leather upper cracked and re-treated until it's almost matte black. A close-cropped knit beanie in faded black, hand-stitched with a small geometric pattern in rust thread at the cuff, sits low over the ears.
materials: heavy thermal weave with aug-channel seams
functionality: Aug-channel shirt accommodates functional chrome arms if the wearer ever acquires them. Layered vest provides moderate impact and abrasion protection. Salvaged chrome bracer protects the forearm from debris and light strikes despite being non-functional internally. Composite-soled boots provide grip and durability on industrial terrain.
what_it_says: This person knows the aug world from the outside — close enough to scavenge its castoffs, far enough away to never afford entry. The chrome accessories are aspirational and confrontational at once, a refusal to be invisible. The hand-stitched beanie is the one thing that's entirely theirs.
worn_by: anyone who moves between the aug trade and the street
manufacturer: Shirt is a Pragma Systems aug-compatible base layer, heavily worn; vest is fully self-constructed; chrome accessories are stripped aug-yard salvage
price_range: Φ20–Φ45 depending on chrome scrap value
story_hooks: One of the salvaged chrome pieces isn't as non-functional as the wearer believes — a faint signal is still broadcasting from the sensor ring, and someone is tracking it.
A Tier 4 chrome-surgeon notices the aug-channel shirt and offers a deal: functional installation of salvaged chrome in exchange for a favor that sounds too easy.
The geometric pattern on the beanie is a territorial marker from a Shelf crew that no longer exists — and an older resident recognizes it, with complicated feelings.

physical_description.visual_profile: A lean, street-hardened silhouette that reads as intentionally salvaged and aug-aspirational. The layered vest creates an asymmetric, weighted appearance — heavier on the left — that suggests both practicality and aesthetic defiance. Chrome accessories catch light against matte darks, creating visual texture without function. Overall impression: someone who lives in the aug-yards and wears that world as identity.
physical_description.fit: Compression-tight base layer with structured arm channels; oversized sleeveless vest that hangs loosely over the torso with deliberate asymmetry; straight-leg industrial trousers with no taper; boots laced snug at the ankle. Layered silhouette creates bulk without bulk — visual density rather than actual weight.
physical_description.primary_material: Pragma Systems thermal weave (graphite base layer); layered salvage composite (conveyor belt rubber, canvas, ballistic panel fragments); recycled industrial denim; treated/re-treated cracked leather boots; salvaged chrome housings (non-functional); hand-knit wool beanie
physical_description.texture: Smooth thermal compression on the base layer with visible aug-channel seaming; rough, riveted patchwork on the vest with intentional texture variety — rubber grip-ridges, canvas weave, ballistic matte finish; distressed, cracked, matte-finished boot leather; hand-knit beanie with loose weave and visible stitch work in contrasting thread
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant graphite and charcoal across base layer and trousers; vest is a visual cacophony of grays, blacks, and industrial tones with no unified hue — rubber blacks, canvas taupes, ballistic grays; chrome components reflect ambient light in cool silvers; rust-colored hand-stitching detail on beanie cuff; black rubber patch on right knee
physical_description.closures: Base layer: friction-fit compression; vest: riveted construction with no closures (hangs open); trousers: standard industrial waistband with belt loops (no visible belt); boots: traditional cross-laced leather with composite eyelets; beanie: pull-on, no fasteners
distinctive_features: Empty aug-channel seams running down both arms of base layer
Asymmetrically weighted salvage-strip vest, heavier on left side
Salvaged non-functional chrome forearm housing worn as right-arm bracer
Defunct sensor ring repurposed as thick wrist cuff on left
Right-knee blowout patched with black rubber on charcoal denim
Cracked, re-treated boot leather with matte finish
Hand-stitched geometric pattern in rust thread at beanie cuff
Riveted construction throughout vest with mixed material textures
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 sub-grade / ungoverned Shelf aesthetic — deliberately salvage-forward, wearing aug-yard materials as both survival and statement. No access to functional chrome, but claiming visual proximity to the augmentation world.
physical_description.cultural_context: Aug-yard scavenger or Shelf dweller. This outfit signals someone who lives in salvage zones, understands chrome disassembly, and has built identity around the materials that corpo-tier discards. It's anti-wealth display — a refusal to hide poverty, instead weaponizing it as aesthetic and knowledge. Wears the breakdown as armor.
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily worn, deliberately patched, weathered but maintained. Nothing is pristine; everything shows use. The vest looks hand-constructed (because it is); the boots show repeated re-treatment; the beanie shows hand-stitching. Worn not despite decay, but because of it — decay is the medium.
